idiom_name: plain JSON link object + global URL + fetch
implementation_notes: TypeScript absorbs the classic structure into three stdlib-grade pieces: the link itself is a plain interface (Link with href plus optional rel-carrying method/type metadata) serialized as JSON, so it crosses every boundary the language already crosses - fetch bodies, Response.json(), structuredClone - with zero custom machinery. The global URL constructor is the resolver: new URL(href, base) validates and resolves relative references against the request's origin, and fetch(url) is the universal dereferencer returning a Promise<Response>. No Link class, factory, or registry type is needed; a Record<LinkRel, Link> member on the response type replaces the classic Link Producer/Carrier/Consumer objects. A fuller abstraction (Ketting, @hateoas-ts) is justified when a client must parse multiple hypermedia formats (HAL, Siren, HTTP Link headers), cache navigated resources, or layer auth middleware over every dereference.
pitfalls: fetch() does NOT reject on HTTP error statuses - only on network failures - so a dead link (the pattern's link-rot tradeoff) resolves normally: always branch on Response.ok/Response.status before res.json(), or 404s flow silently into downstream logic.

href is typed as string but the type system cannot constrain what it points at; treat new URL(href, base) (throws TypeError on malformed input) as the validation gate, and never treat a received href as an authorization grant - enforce auth at resolution time and sign or scope links that cross trust boundaries.

Emitting absolute URLs leaks internal hostnames and ports: produce relative hrefs at the edge and resolve them per environment with new URL(href, request.url origin) instead of baking an API host constant into serialized responses.

Following links without validating the relation type and method: a 'describedby' or 'related' link is not safe to mutate - gate dereference on the rel string (typed as a keyof union over the _links map) and the declared method before calling fetch.

res.json() is only a Promise<any> annotation - an absent _links member yields undefined at runtime no matter how precise the interface looks; navigation helpers should return Link | undefined so missing relations surface in the type flow instead of exploding at pay.href.

Late-bound dereferencing inherits the caller's AbortSignal lifetime: a link followed after the originating request's signal fired throws AbortError immediately, and cyclic next-link pagination needs a visited-URL guard or the async iteration never terminates.
